occupational_domain: Information Systems, human-computer interaction, and interaction design

evidence.quote: Last year I led a redesign of our onboarding wizard, aiming to cut first-week drop-off.
evidence.explanation: The core work episode is planning and executing a multi-stage redesign project involving sequencing of vendor selection, contractor hiring, experimentation, and technical migration decisions toward a goal within a fixed window.

evidence.quote: We still had roughly six weeks left, so a one-sprint migration wouldn't have threatened the review date at all.
evidence.explanation: The participant weighs timing, dependencies, and resource tradeoffs between continuing customization and migrating, which is planning under constraints rather than a routine next step.

secondary_categories.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: three research vendor proposals came in... I had plenty of time to sit with these
evidence.explanation: The participant gathers and evaluates competing vendor proposals against price, features, and scope.

evidence.quote: Two candidates: one had flagship work at a well-known unicorn startup... The other had a plainer portfolio but included actual test scripts, metrics, iteration logs.
evidence.explanation: Evaluating competing contractor portfolios and evidence of competence is an information-evaluation task.

evidence.quote: six thousand dollars, five sessions... twenty-one thousand for ten sessions... twenty-three thousand for twelve sessions
evidence.explanation: Comparing costs, session counts, and value ratios across proposals requires numerical reasoning.

evidence.quote: a hundred forty users... the sample was under our significance threshold
evidence.explanation: Interpreting sample size and statistical significance is a numeracy-based task.

evidence.quote: That my adjustments were doing something.
evidence.explanation: The participant forms a causal model linking a manual intervention to an observed metric change, an act of abstraction and explanation-building, even though the model is later shown to be unconfirmed.

evidence.quote: I asked the Analytics Lead for more manual control so I could keep pushing on it.
evidence.explanation: Coordinating with the Analytics Lead over control of a shared system and negotiating access reflects managing dependencies across roles.

evidence.quote: I argued to keep customizing the legacy piece.
evidence.explanation: Advocating for a technical direction in coordination with engineering reflects cross-functional coordination and prioritization.

A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct end-user service interaction described in this episode
A3.2 Teaching, training, coaching - no instructional activity described

A3.3 Selling and influencing - the argument to keep the legacy component borders on advocacy, but insufficient evidence of persuasion of another party's decision is shown beyond a stated internal position
A3.5 Caring - not applicable to this episode
ambiguities: The legacy-component argument (decision point 4) could be read as A3.3 Selling/influencing (advocating a position to stakeholders) or as A2.6 Creativity/resolution (a design-continuation judgment); the text shows the participant's internal reasoning and a stated argument but does not show the persuasion exchange with another party, so it was not elevated to a full secondary category.

A2.2 Literacy is present in the interview format itself (talking, reading proposals, portfolios) but is not separately evidenced as a distinct meaningful work activity beyond information evaluation, so it was folded into A2.4 rather than listed separately.
